policy: Never mark an experiment COMPLETED unless its required dataset exists and the experiment executed successfully. Human experiments must remain in HUMAN_DATA_REQUIRED until actual empirical participants are evaluated.

experiments.title: Document Ingestion & Chunking Evaluation
experiments.research_question: Can academic engineering documents (PDF, PPTX, TXT) be ingested and chunked with exact character boundary provenance and NFC normalization?
experiments.hypothesis: Recursive character chunking preserves sentence and character boundaries while maintaining Indic Unicode normalization.
experiments.dataset: Synthetic academic lecture notes and course slides
experiments.procedure: Ingest documents, extract text, clean Unicode, split recursively, verify character offsets against original file.
experiments.limitations: Tested on clean synthetic engineering notes; scanned PDF OCR not evaluated.

experiments.title: Cross-Lingual Academic Retrieval Evaluation
experiments.research_question: Which dense embedding and hybrid retrieval architecture best retrieves English course chunks for Telugu, Romanized Telugu, and code-mixed student queries?
experiments.hypothesis: Multilingual E5 small with RRF hybrid fusion will outperform pure lexical baselines on cross-lingual retrieval.
experiments.procedure: Index 10 course chunks in vector and BM25 stores; evaluate 40 queries across EN, TE, te-Latn, te-en across multiple retrievers.
experiments.limitations: Evaluated on introductory Signals and Systems corpus; advanced domain transfer unmeasured.

experiments.title: Academic Concept & Relation Extraction Evaluation
experiments.research_question: How accurately can academic concepts, aliases, and directional prerequisite relations be extracted from course text?
experiments.hypothesis: Rule-based and heading-aware extraction will capture foundational curriculum concepts with high recall against gold standards.
experiments.procedure: Run concept extractor on textbook chunks; compare extracted graph against single-expert gold graph.
experiments.limitations: Evaluated against single-expert annotated gold standard; inter-annotator agreement unmeasured.

experiments.title: Indic NLP & Cross-Lingual Concept Mapping Evaluation
experiments.research_question: Can student queries across English, Telugu script, Romanized Telugu, and code-mixed text be mapped to canonical graph concept IDs?
experiments.hypothesis: Hybrid concept mapping fusing graph terminology detection, lexical normalization, and dense embeddings will achieve higher Recall@1 than exact matching.
experiments.procedure: Detect language and code-mixing, normalize Romanized text, extract technical terms, score concept candidates via hybrid fusion.
experiments.limitations: Heuristic transliteration dictionary covers core engineering terminology; rare dialectal forms not covered.

experiments.title: RAG Pipeline & Grounded Answer Generation Baseline
experiments.research_question: Does concept-aware retrieval and citation verification provide grounded answers while flagging insufficient evidence?
experiments.hypothesis: Concept expansion improves evidence recall on Indic queries; citation validation detects ungrounded claims.
experiments.procedure: Execute full RAG pipeline across 24 queries; evaluate multi-chunk retrieval, fallback on unanswerable queries, and citation correctness.
experiments.limitations: Evaluated with MockLLMProvider for offline deterministic reproducibility.

experiments.title: Research-Hardened RAG Multi-Ablation Evaluation
experiments.research_question: How do knowledge graph context and query normalization formulations contribute to multi-chunk cross-lingual retrieval?
experiments.hypothesis: Canonical concept expansion will improve retrieval recall; unbudgeted graph context may cause candidate displacement.
experiments.procedure: Run 60 expanded queries across 3 difficulty tiers and 4 language varieties; execute graph and query formulation ablations.
experiments.limitations: Revealed 5/10 false acceptances on adversarial out-of-scope queries (resolved in EXP-005B).

experiments.title: RAG Safety, Scope Control & Retrieval Hardening
experiments.research_question: Can multi-signal scope assessment prevent adversarial keyword-bait false acceptances and eliminate graph candidate displacement?
experiments.hypothesis: Generic term penalties and concept margin checks will achieve zero false acceptances on out-of-scope queries; post-retrieval graph context will preserve 0.9200 Recall@5.
experiments.procedure: Evaluate 45 queries (in-scope, out-of-scope, ambiguous); decouple graph enrichment to post-retrieval prompt context.
experiments.limitations: Tested on curated adversarial engineering benchmark.

experiments.title: Student Knowledge Model Invariants & Audit
experiments.research_question: Do evidence-weighted knowledge updates, recency decay, and mastery rules maintain mathematical monotonicity and multi-student isolation?
experiments.hypothesis: Assessments dominate observational questions; conflicting signals stabilize in UNCERTAIN status; Student A updates never alter Student B.
experiments.procedure: Execute 10 controlled interaction sequences (monotonic, recovery, weak restraint, cold start); audit and verify all 27 mathematical invariants.
experiments.limitations: Heuristic evidence-weighted model; not calibrated against empirical human learning curves.

experiments.title: Adaptive Assessment Core Selection Evaluation
experiments.research_question: Does policy-driven adaptive assessment correctly target weakness, uncertainty, and prerequisites while avoiding repetition?
experiments.hypothesis: Multi-signal candidate scoring prioritizes unmastered foundational concepts; difficulty matches student state; chunk provenance is preserved.
experiments.procedure: Run 10 controlled assessment scenarios with 16 grounded question items across EASY, MEDIUM, HARD tiers and 4 languages.
experiments.limitations: Controlled question bank; live generative question generation deferred.

experiments.title: Personalized Recommendations & Remediation Evaluation
experiments.research_question: Can multi-signal prioritization and decoupled pedagogical actions guide students toward unmastered prerequisites and practice without false deficit labeling?
experiments.hypothesis: Weakness scaled by confidence prioritizes validated failure; cold-start triggers review without deficit labels; unindexed concepts flag SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.
experiments.procedure: Evaluate 12 controlled student states (weakness, uncertainty, blocker, recency damping, mastered deprioritization, isolation).
experiments.limitations: Evaluates recommendation algorithm consistency; student learning gains unmeasured.

experiments.title: Student Dashboard & Knowledge Map Interface Invariants
experiments.research_question: Does the presentation layer maintain strict view-layer decoupling, provenance preservation, student isolation, and reactive state refresh?
experiments.hypothesis: The client performs zero scoring; SVG map renders canonical concepts; answering quizzes refreshes state without server crashes.
experiments.procedure: Execute 15 controlled API and interface scenarios via FastAPI TestClient.
experiments.limitations: Evaluates software interface contracts; human usability trials unmeasured.

experiments.title: Controlled Recommendation Rule-Consistency Benchmark
experiments.research_question: Do recommendation candidates, action types, and reason codes strictly adhere to rule-consistency contracts under diverse student profiles?
experiments.hypothesis: Decoupled pedagogical action selector consistently maps prerequisite deficits to REVIEW_PREREQUISITE and uncertain concepts to diagnostic assessment.
experiments.procedure: Execute 10 controlled student scenarios testing edge cases in recommendation planning and verify rule compliance.
experiments.limitations: Controlled software rule evaluation; does not evaluate pedagogical efficacy.

experiments.title: Controlled Adaptive Assessment Core Benchmark
experiments.research_question: Does the adaptive assessment engine consistently match difficulty, maintain provenance, and avoid session item repetition across multilingual questions?
experiments.hypothesis: Item difficulty tracks student knowledge score thresholds; language selection respects preferences with English fallback; determinism is preserved.
experiments.procedure: Execute 10 controlled adaptive testing scenarios evaluating candidate generation, item selection, deterministic grading, and evidence emission.
experiments.limitations: Controlled question bank evaluation; psychometric IRT calibration unmeasured.

experiments.title: Dashboard Usability Evaluation Framework
experiments.research_question: How clearly do engineering students understand knowledge map navigation, evidence transparency, and model-estimated states?
experiments.hypothesis: The visual graph combined with the 'Why this estimate?' transparency panel enables students to interpret estimated states without psychological confusion.
experiments.procedure: Administer 9 standard tasks (T1-T9) to engineering students followed by 6-item neutral Likert usability questionnaire.
experiments.limitations: Human participants not yet recruited; returns HUMAN_DATA_REQUIRED.

experiments.title: RAG Human Annotation & Attribution Analysis
experiments.research_question: How do human evaluators rate generated answer factual correctness, evidence support, and citation integrity across language varieties?
experiments.hypothesis: Answers grounded in retrieved academic chunks will achieve higher evidence support ratings than ungrounded completions.
experiments.procedure: Independent human annotators rate model-generated answers on 1-5 scales following explicit annotation guidelines.
experiments.limitations: Human annotators not yet recruited; returns HUMAN_DATA_REQUIRED.

experiments.title: Multilingual Human Evaluation by Language Variety
experiments.research_question: How do native Telugu-speaking engineering students evaluate pedagogical clarity and technical term naturalness across English, Telugu, Romanized Telugu, and code-mixed formulations?
experiments.hypothesis: Code-mixed formulations preserving English technical terms with Telugu grammatical scaffolding will be rated higher in pedagogical clarity than pure Telugu translations of technical jargon.
experiments.procedure: Evaluate per-language cohorts across 4 linguistic formulations; compute disaggregated descriptive metrics and non-parametric rank comparisons.
experiments.limitations: Human evaluators not yet recruited; returns HUMAN_DATA_REQUIRED.
